# 4 Maccabees Chapter 12 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Brothers' Inner Resolve and Praise

---

**1** For truly the contest in which they were involved was a divine one, and the virtue by which they were tested was the virtue of patient endurance.

**2** The prizes for which they were contending were incorruptible prizes of immortality and undying glory.

**3** But even if none of those things had been true — even if the law had promised no reward — their reason alone would have been worthy to earn them the crown of virtue.

**4** For they suffered for virtue's sake, and they overcame the tyrant through the power of reason.

**5** The seven brothers are more admirable than the greatest heroes — for they mastered passion not with weapons of iron but with the weapons of noble reason.

**6** They are more victorious than those who fought at Thermopylae — for the Spartans fought with iron weapons, but these men fought with the weapons of reason and virtue.

**7** The noble Eleazar is the first champion in battle, the mother of the seven is the second in command, and the seven brothers form the sacred company.

**8** The tyrant was their adversary, the world was their arena, and devotion to God was their weapon.

**9** Their praise has gone out into all the world, for they lived the life of virtue and died for the law.

**10** For in dying for righteousness they gained life and fame that shall never end.

**11** They proved that reason is the true master of the passions, not only in principle but in the reality of their deaths.

**12** They showed that piety is truly indestructible when it is put to the ultimate test.

**13** O mother, what words are adequate to praise you fittingly? You bore witness to the faithfulness of the law in your very body.

**14** By your own death you put the seal on the proof that reason is master of the passions.

**15** For you, like a wrestler in the arena, endured every blow of the tyrant's passion and were not thrown down.

**16** You held firm; you did not waver; you proved the sovereignty of reason over passion in your very flesh.

**17** For as long as our nation endures, the memory of Eleazar and the seven brothers and their mother will be imperishable.

**18** Happy are those who received this honor! For they are now at rest with God and with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

**19** The blessed ones proved by the nobility of their dying that reason can master the passions.

**20** Here I conclude my argument: devotion to God, through the instruction of reason, is sovereign over all the passions.

**21** This is proved by the heroic deaths of Eleazar and the seven brothers and the mother who was worthy of them.

**22** Let no one despise the weakness of old age or the tenderness of youth in matters of virtue — for these heroes prove that neither age nor youth is an obstacle to virtue.
